work.title: Piano Sonata No. 30 in E major

version.note: The edition Schnabel played from is not identified in the recording sources.

date.note: The Internet Archive description gives “recorded 22.III.1932” for the Op. 109 sonata and the Naxos Historical review gives 22 March 1932 for the same session; the Commons date field says only 1932.

place.note: Given for the whole sonata in the review of the Naxos Historical reissue.

catalogue.note: The catalogue span identifies the original complete-sonata issue (the sonata runs about twenty minutes). Which sides carry this movement is not established, and the span is not shown to be the physical source of the Internet Archive MP3.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take or side information is established for this movement.

credits.note: The transfer engineer of the Internet Archive MP3 is not identified. Mark Obert-Thorn is credited for the separate Naxos reissue, not for this transfer.

date.note: No transfer date is documented; the Internet Archive item was added in March 2020 and the Commons file in January 2021, which are upload dates.

processing.value: Internet Archive original: 256 kbps MP3, track 095 of Beethoven Piano Sonatas vol. 8; Commons holds an Ogg Vorbis conversion and supplies an MP3 derivative.
processing.note: No restoration settings or original transfer chain are documented.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Beethoven died in 1827. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to Schnabel’s 1932 HMV recording and the Internet Archive item carries a Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL. The programme’s pre-1963 European rule applies because the 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. The exact first-publication date is not independently documented.

alternatives.value: PD-EU-audio — European performers’ and producers’ rights claimed expired.
Public Domain Mark 1.0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item.

rights.creditLine: Ludwig van Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 30, Op. 109, II. Prestissimo; Artur Schnabel, piano, HMV, Abbey Road Studio No. 3, 22 March 1932. Internet Archive (Beethoven Piano Sonatas vol. 8) via Wikimedia Commons. Commons asserts EU public-domain recording status (PD-EU-audio); rights elsewhere are not established.
